title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 750–752 of the continuation of La Longue Marche): Grothendieck is axiomatizing a datum (32) made of the following pieces.
- A profinite group M.
- A closed normal subgroup 𝔊 with quotient Γ = M/𝔊.
- A normal subgroup π of 𝔊.
- Dense discrete subgroups π_0 ⊂ 𝔊_0 of π ⊂ 𝔊, with Γ_0 = 𝔊_0/π_0.
On the previous page Γ_0 plays the role of a discrete Teichmüller group, its completion that of a profinite Teichmüller group, and Γ that of a profinite Galois group. He singles out two extreme cases: (a) 𝔊_0 = π_0, the case of a smooth multiplicity (stack) over a field of finite type over Q; (b) 𝔊_0/π_0 equal to (a finite-index subgroup of) the Teichmüller group of π_0, the 'modular' case.

This page finishes (b). In the modular case:
- M is the arithmetic fundamental group of a suitable modular multiplicity (a moduli stack such as M_{g,n} over Q).
- 𝔊 is its 'geometric' part, π_1 over Q̄.
- 𝔊_0 is its 'transcendental' part, the topological orbifold π_1, i.e. a discrete mapping-class/Teichmüller group.
- Γ is Gal(Q̄/Q).

He then imposes a hypothesis on (32). The cyclotomic character on M (M acts on π by outer automorphisms of the 'L-structure', i.e. the surface-group lien) is trivial on 𝔊, so it factors through Γ. Equivalently (33), π = π^+ and 𝔊 = 𝔊^+: the geometric groups lie in the orientation-preserving part, the kernel of the character. This gives (34): χ_Γ : Γ → Ẑ^*. He crossed out a clause requiring the image of χ_Γ to be open.

Next he takes a pair (G_Q, χ_G) from (17), p. 748: an algebraic group over Q with a character χ_G, the analogue of GSp with its multiplier. He considers adelic homomorphisms M → G(A_Q) satisfying conditions 1°–4°, where 3° is strengthened to '3° forte': compatibility with the discreteness of the Teichmüller group 𝔊_0. That is, the restriction to 𝔊_0 factors through G(Q), giving the commutative square (31) on the next page: 𝔊_0 ↪ M, 𝔊_0 → G(Q) ↪ G(A_Q).

On the next page he names data (32) 'structures de Galois–Teichmüller' and such a homomorphism a 'lien de Lie'. He then introduces the Q-group scheme M_Q and the subgroup scheme 𝔊_Q 'generated by' the image, i.e. an algebraic (Zariski) hull.

Model case: moduli of curves or abelian varieties. Here π_1^arith(M_g) → GSp_{2g}(A_f), with Sp_{2g}(Z) ⊂ Sp_{2g}(Q) on the discrete part and the multiplier equal to the cyclotomic character. The aim is a 'linearized' (algebraic-group) shadow of the Galois action on Teichmüller groups, with a rational structure coming from the topological fundamental group.
errors: The transcription's 'se factorise par π' must mean 'factors through Γ'. A character trivial on 𝔊 factors through M/𝔊 = Γ, which is exactly what (34) states, so this is a reading/transcription slip, not a mathematical error.

M → G(A_Q) presumably really lands in G(A_f) (finite adeles), since M is profinite and any continuous map to the archimedean factor is trivial on the connected part. This is a harmless imprecision in the notes.

The marginal note on the next page ('Oublié par la suite à introduire les conditions de discontinuité') shows Grothendieck himself noting a gap: the discreteness conditions on the structure itself were not built into the definition (32).

ideas.what: Abstract axiomatic 'Galois–Teichmüller structure': a profinite M with geometric part 𝔊, Galois quotient Γ, and discrete 'transcendental' dense subgroup 𝔊_0 (a Teichmüller group). Modelled on π_1^arith of moduli stacks.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic vs geometric vs topological fundamental groups of M_{g,n}; Galois–Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme 1984); developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps, Lochak, Matsumoto
ideas.where_published: Galois–Teichmüller theory programme in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific axiomatic datum (32) appears only in these notes as far as known

ideas.what: Cyclotomic character of the arithmetic π_1 acting on the surface lien, assumed trivial on the geometric part, so that it factors through Gal(Q̄/Q) → Ẑ^* and the geometric groups are orientation-preserving (π = π^+).
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic character via the action on the inertia/orientation class of the surface group
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses orientation and the cyclotomic character

ideas.what: 'Lie links': adelic representations M → G(A_Q) of the arithmetic fundamental group, compatible with a character χ_G ↔ cyclotomic character. They satisfy a strong rationality condition: the discrete Teichmüller group maps into G(Q). Followed by the algebraic group scheme generated by the image.
ideas.modern_name: Relative/weighted completion of mapping class groups and Galois groups; adelic monodromy of the symplectic local system on M_g (cf. Shimura-type data)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain (relative completion, 1990s), Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2003; relative pro-ℓ completion of mapping class groups, 2009); Deligne (motivic π_1, 1989)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes studying the Galois action on Teichmüller groups through adelic linear representations M → G(A_Q). Their restriction to the discrete Teichmüller group is required to be Q-rational, and he then takes the algebraic group generated by the image. This is essentially the framework later made precise as relative/weighted completion (Hain, Hain–Matsumoto). There, Γ_g → Sp_{2g}(Q) and Gal(Q̄/Q) → GSp_{2g}(Q_ℓ) are used to build proalgebraic hulls of π_1^arith(M_g). Grothendieck's version is adelic rather than ℓ-adic and axiomatic (any (G, χ_G)). It is also tied explicitly to the cyclotomic character as the multiplier.
missed.quote: on s'intéresse aux homomorphismes M → G(A_Q) satisfaisant les conditions 1°) 2°) 3°) 4°) ... (3° forte) (compatibilité aux discontinuités de Teichmüller 𝔊_0)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This shows Grothendieck anticipating the 'linearization' of Galois–Teichmüller theory around 1981–82, a decade before Hain's relative completion. The adelic, all-primes-at-once and axiomatic formulation ('lien de Lie' for an abstract Galois–Teichmüller structure) is not the standard one and could be of historical and some conceptual interest.

missed.claim: The abstract notion of a 'Galois–Teichmüller structure' (32) and of its 'Lie links' is defined but, by Grothendieck's own marginal note, the discreteness conditions were left incomplete. No developed theory of these abstract structures exists in the literature.
missed.quote: Les structures de la forme (32) méritent sans doute un nom ... structures de Galois-Teichmüller
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a possible axiomatic framework unifying the Shimura-variety-type adelic monodromy and Galois actions on mapping class groups. It is only modest, since the concrete cases are well studied.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sketches an adelic, axiomatic 'Lie link' formalism for Galois actions on Teichmüller groups. It includes Q-rationality of the topological part and an algebraic hull, which prefigures Hain–Matsumoto relative/weighted completion. Interesting historically, but the ideas are in spirit present in later literature, and the page is a definitional sketch.
transcription_corrections: First word is 'M' (Grothendieck's script M for the big group), not 'Π': 'M s'interprète comme le groupe fondamental d'une multiplicité modulaire convenable'.
'T comme sa partie géométrique' should read '𝔊 comme sa partie géométrique', and 'T_0' should read '𝔊_0' (Grothendieck's gothic G).
'Γ comme π_{Q̄/Q}' (the Galois group of Q̄ over Q).
'la condition cyclotomique' is likely 'le caractère cyclotomique sur M'.
'triviale sur G, i.e. se factorise par π' should be 'trivial sur 𝔊, i.e. se factorise par Γ' (consistent with (34)). G here and in (33) is 𝔊: '(33) π = π^+, 𝔊 = 𝔊^+'.
Crossed-out line: 'dont l'image soit un sous-groupe ouvert'.
'(compatibilité aux discontinuités de Teichmüller 𝔊_0)' is probably 'compatibilité aux discrétisations de Teichmüller 𝔊_0'.
'L-structures' is uncertain; it possibly refers to lien (outer action) structures.
